newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dasa starts talks with Matra.
newsitem.headline: Dasa starts talks with Matra.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa) has begun cooperation talks with France's Matra, and is mulling whether to end its discussions with Aerospatiale, chairman Manfred Bischoff was reported on Thursday as saying.
Bischoff's remarks are the first on-the-record reaction by Dasa, Germany's main defence company, to France's plans to sell the defence operations of Thomson SA to Lagardere.

In a privatisation still awaiting approval from a special commission, Lagardere wants to merge Thomson SA's defence unit Thomson CSF with its own Matra missile unit to create one of the world's biggest defence groups.
"We are right at the start of negotiations over possible cooperation in the areas of defence electronics and guided missiles," the Handelsblatt daily quoted Bischoff telling a briefing.
Bischoff said that he did not rule out the possibility of some form of cross-shareholding.
The new negotiations will force a review of talks between Dasa and Aerospatiale, Handelsblatt said.
The two companies have been negotiating for over two years on merging their satellite and missile operations, but have not yet closed a deal.
French Defence Minister Charles Millon said in mid-October that the expected Lagardere takeover of Thomson would not call into question the Dasa-Aerospatiale talks.
Defence relations between Germany and France, already strained by constraints on Bonn's military budget, will be on the agenda of a Franco-German summit on December 9 in Nuremberg.
No comment was immediately available from Dasa's Munich headquarters.
